summary: Weather Machine is a dense Vital Lacerda puzzle where players manage overlapping tracks and resource conversions to tune the weather while dodging an escalating side-effect mechanism that threatens to shut down their machine. Turns require careful action-point planning across a personal player board packed with interlocking systems, and the game rewards chaining several actions into a single efficient turn.
praised: intricate, tightly interlocking systems typical of Lacerda designs
beautiful, functional player boards and iconography
strong sense of progression as your machine becomes more efficient
criticised: very steep learning curve and long teach
mostly solitaire-feeling turns with limited direct interaction
high cost and heavy production may be daunting for casual groups

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with shared resource/market competition
interaction.detail: Each player operates their own machine and board almost independently, with interaction limited to competing for shared market slots, turn order, and end-game scoring positions rather than direct conflict.

scoring.why: Points come from multiple interlocking tracks (weather effects, contracts, side-effect management, and end-game bonuses), rewarding a well-balanced engine over a single strategy.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by building the most efficient personal engine, converting resources into completed weather effects and contracts faster and cleaner than your opponents while limiting harmful side effects.
